---
title: Make tools with Copilot
description: "Describe a tool, such as one that makes images with your OpenAI key, and Copilot writes it as an MCP server that chat can use. Try it, change it, and share it."
---

> [!WARNING]
> Making tools with Copilot is an experiment. Turn it on in **Settings → Experiments** with **Make
> tools with Copilot**. It may change or be removed in a future update.

When chat needs something no MCP server does, make a tool for it. Describe what the tool should do,
such as make pictures for your app with OpenAI's image model, and Copilot writes it. Fabricator
checks that it starts, then adds it to your MCP servers, so you turn it on in an app's chat like any
other server. See [Connect MCP servers](/docs/build/mcp-servers).

## How a tool you make works

A tool you make is a small MCP server written in JavaScript. Fabricator keeps its code on this
computer and runs it with Node.js, which Fabricator already needs. Each tool can offer several
tools of its own, such as `make_image`, that chat calls while it builds your app.

- **It runs in your app's folder.** When chat uses it, the tool runs in the folder of the app you're
  building, so a file it saves, such as a picture in `public/images`, is part of your app.
- **It uses your keys.** A tool gets the keys it needs, such as an API key, as environment variables.
  Fabricator keeps their values in Windows Credential Manager, or in your Keychain on macOS, and
  Copilot only ever sees their names.
- **It's yours.** Like the servers you add, the tools you make are on this computer only. They aren't
  saved with an app.

## Make a tool

1. Open **Settings**, and select **Manage MCP servers**. Or, in an app's chat composer, select
   **Plugins**, then **Make a tool with Copilot…**, and skip the next step.
2. Select **Make a tool with Copilot**.
3. Under **What should it do?**, describe the tool: what it does, which service it uses, and what it
   gives back. Copilot can read the service's documentation on the web while it works. To start
   from an idea, select one under **Start from an idea:**, such as **Make images**, which fills in
   the description and the key it needs.
4. Under **Name**, enter a name, such as `Image maker`, or leave it empty and Copilot names the
   tool.
5. Under **Keys**, add the keys it needs:
   - To use a key you saved in **Accounts → Model providers**, such as your OpenAI key, select
     **Use a key from Model providers**, then the key. The tool gets that key, and changing the key
     in Model providers changes it for the tool too.
   - For any other key, select **Add variable**, then enter its name, such as `STABILITY_API_KEY`,
     and its value. You can leave the value empty and add it once the tool is made.
6. Choose a **Model** for Copilot to write the tool with, or leave it on **Auto**.
7. Select **Make tool**, or press Ctrl+Enter (⌘Enter on macOS).

```prompt title="An image tool on your OpenAI key"
Make an image from a description with OpenAI's latest image model, and save it as a PNG in the
app's public/images folder, at a path chat chooses. Let chat pick the size (square, wide or tall)
and the quality (low, medium or high, low by default). Return the path it saved.
```

Copy the text above into **What should it do?**, and add your OpenAI key under **Keys**.

While Copilot works, Fabricator shows how long it has taken and where it is: **Plan**, **Read
docs**, **Write code** and **Check**, with the model it runs on, the pages it read and the lines it
wrote. Under the headline, you see what Copilot says as it works. Below, you see your request while
Copilot starts, the pages as it reads them, then the tool's code as Copilot writes it. When
Fabricator checks that the tool starts and it doesn't, Copilot reads why and fixes it; select
**Details** to see what went wrong. Making a tool usually takes a minute or two. If you close the
dialog while Copilot works, Fabricator asks whether to stop it first.

When it's done, you see what Copilot says about the tool and the tools it offers. Copilot writes
the tool's name, if you left it to Copilot, and what it says in the language you described the tool
in. Select **What Copilot did** to see each step again.

If the tool's code reads a key you didn't add, or one you left empty, Fabricator says "Its code
reads `<KEY>`, which it doesn't get yet." Select **Add keys** and enter its value.

To use the tool in the app you have open, select **Use in this chat**, which turns it on in the
app's chat and closes the dialog. To use it in another app, turn it on in that app's chat: in the
chat composer, select **Plugins**, and under **MCP servers**, turn it on. See
[Turn a server on in a chat](/docs/build/mcp-servers#turn-a-server-on-in-a-chat).

```prompt title="Use the image tool"
Add a hero picture to the home page: a calm harbor at sunrise, wide, made with Image maker and saved
in public/images/hero.png.
```

## Try a tool

Try a tool before chat uses it, to see that it works with your keys.

1. In **MCP servers**, select **Try** on the tool.
2. If it offers more than one tool, choose one.
3. Fill in its arguments, or select **Edit as JSON** to enter them as JSON.
4. Select **Run**.

The tool runs with its keys, in a folder of its own that stands in for an app's folder. You see what
it returned, and the files it saved, with a picture of each image. Select **Open folder** to see
everything it saved. A service the tool uses may charge you for each try, as it does when chat uses
the tool. The next time you try a tool, its form starts with what you last ran it with, until you
close Fabricator. Press Ctrl+Enter (⌘Enter on macOS) to run it again.

## Change a tool

1. In **MCP servers**, select **Change** on the tool. Select **What you asked for before** to see
   the requests it was made and changed from.
2. Under **What should change?**, describe the change, such as "Let chat choose a transparent
   background."
3. Select **Change tool**.

Copilot starts from the tool's code and what you asked for before. Fabricator keeps the change only
once the tool starts, and the next message in each chat that has the tool on uses it. If the change
isn't what you wanted, select **Undo change** to put the tool back as it was.

To change its name or its keys, select **Edit** instead.

## Read a tool's code

In **MCP servers**, select **Code** on the tool to read its code and what you asked for when it was
made and changed. Select **Open folder** to open the folder the code is in. You can change the code
there yourself: select **Check** on the tool afterwards to see that it still starts.

After Copilot changes a tool, select **Last change** to see what changed in its code. To put the
tool back as it was before the change, select **Undo change**, then **Undo change** again to
confirm. Only the last change can be undone.

## Share a tool

1. In **MCP servers**, select **Export** on the tool.
2. Choose where to save the file, which ends in `.fabricator-tool.json`.

The file holds the tool's name, what it does, its code, and the names of its keys. It never holds a
key's value. To add a tool someone shared with you:

1. In **MCP servers**, select **Add a shared tool…**, and choose its file.
2. Read what it does and its code.
3. Enter your own keys, or use one from **Model providers**.
4. Select **Add tool**.

Fabricator adds it once it starts.

## What a tool can do

- **A tool runs with your access.** Like any command server, a tool runs on this computer with your
  access to it and your accounts. Read the code of a tool someone shared before you add it.
- **Copilot works only on the tool.** While it makes a tool, Copilot can read pages on the web and
  save the tool, nothing else: it can't read your files, run commands or see your keys. Fabricator
  starts each version on its own, without your keys, and doesn't call its tools.
- **Chat decides when to call it.** Chat uses a tool only when a request needs it, and a tool that
  changes something outside your app only when you ask for that. To let chat call only the tools
  that read, select **Edit** on the tool and select **Only tools that read**. See
  [What chat does with a server's tools](/docs/build/mcp-servers#what-chat-does-with-a-servers-tools).
- **Turning the experiment off** hides making, changing, trying and sharing tools. The tools you made
  stay among your MCP servers, and chats that have them on keep using them.

## A tool doesn't work

- **"Copilot couldn't make a tool that starts."** Copilot tried twice, and the tool still didn't
  start. Select **Edit request** to describe the tool in more detail, such as the service's API or
  the model to use, then select **Make tool** again.
- **"Fabricator needs Node.js to run the tools you make, and it isn't on this computer."** Install
  Node.js, then try again. See [Setup](/docs/start/setup).
- **A try says a key isn't set.** The tool's code reads a key it doesn't get. Select **Edit** on the
  tool, add the key, and select **Save**.
- **"Your OpenAI key isn't in Accounts → Model providers anymore."** The tool uses a key you removed
  from Model providers. Add the key there again, or select **Edit** on the tool and give the variable
  a value of its own.

If it still fails, [Report a problem](/docs/troubleshooting/report-a-problem).
